title: Discrete semiclassical theory of quantum-thermal escape
summary: The dissipationless quantum-thermal escape rate from a metastable well is often written as a Boltzmann average of the Hill-Wheeler flux over a continuum of energies. This continuum treatment diverges exponentially at low temperature, because it pairs the quantum partition function of the well with a classical flux integral. Retaining the discrete nature of the quasibound spectrum removes the divergence exactly, and the resulting rate is obtained in closed form on both sides of the crossover temperature $T_0$. Evaluating a uniform Kemble transmission probability on Bohr-Sommerfeld levels…
